prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (ideological framing removed)

Economy, tax and business
- Fiscal rules: balance day-to-day spending and have debt falling by year five; all major fiscal events audited by the OBR; Covid fraud recovery drive.
- No rises to National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT; abolish non‑dom status; close carried‑interest loophole; modernise HMRC to tackle avoidance.
- Industrial strategy with a statutory council; National Wealth Fund to crowd in private investment (ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, hydrogen); pensions reform to boost productive investment.
- Business tax stability: cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; permanent full expensing and AIA; publish a multi‑year business tax roadmap; replace business rates in England.
- Infrastructure: 10‑year plan; new delivery authority; planning reform for housing, labs and energy; nationwide gigabit and 5G by 2030.
- Transport: maintain and renew roads; fix more potholes; restore 2030 ICE phase‑out; expand EV charging; bring rail into public ownership as contracts expire; empower bus franchising and municipal ownership; integrated local transport.
- Devolution: landmark legislation, Local Growth Plans, multi‑year council settlements; stronger local audit.

Energy, climate and environment
- Zero‑carbon electricity by 2030: expand wind and solar; invest in CCUS, hydrogen and marine; extend nuclear (including SMRs); maintain a strategic gas reserve.
- No new North Sea exploration licences; retain existing licences; ban fracking and new coal.
- Tighten and extend the windfall tax; create a public clean‑power company to co‑invest; local power projects.
- Warm Homes Plan to upgrade five million homes; raise private rental efficiency standards by 2030; upgrade the grid and strengthen energy regulation.
- Nature and water: expand habitats, new river walks and forests; put failing water firms under special measures with tougher fines, bonus bans and criminal sanctions; carbon border adjustment; animal‑welfare bans (e.g., hunting trophies, snares).

Borders, security, policing and justice
- Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; maintain the nuclear deterrent; Martyn’s Law; updated counter‑extremism and hostile‑state response.
- New Border Security Command; more asylum caseworkers; end hotel use; new returns unit; seek EU security agreement; faster removals to safe countries.
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; new powers on antisocial behaviour; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; knife‑crime plan with mandatory interventions and online‑sale controls; youth hubs; specialist rape units and courts; higher policing standards; prison‑building, reoffending reduction and probation reform; strengthened anti‑fraud strategy.

Work, welfare, housing and rights
- Employment reforms: day‑one rights, ban exploitative zero‑hours and fire‑and‑rehire; Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage to reflect living costs and remove age bands.
- Review Universal Credit; national child‑poverty strategy; free breakfast clubs in all primary schools.
- Renters’ reform: abolish Section 21, empower challenges to unreasonable rent hikes, extend Awaab’s Law; overhaul leasehold toward commonhold; building‑safety action; homelessness strategy.
- Equality measures: socio‑economic duty; Race Equality Act; disability and ethnicity pay‑gap reporting; full ban on conversion practices; modernised gender recognition with clinical safeguards; hate‑crime reforms.

Education and skills
- 6,500 teachers in key subjects; restore support‑staff negotiating body; curriculum and assessment review; early numeracy and language programmes; mental‑health support in every school.
- 3,000 school‑based nurseries; parental‑leave review; youth guarantee (18–21).
- Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy to a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; broader access to arts/sport; football regulator; ticket‑resale protections.

Health and social care
- Cut waiting times: 2m extra operations/scans/appointments annually; shared waiting lists; use spare independent capacity.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver hospital building programme; enhance NHS app; regulate managers; new clinical leadership college.
- Primary care: more GPs; face‑to‑face option; pharmacist prescribing; wider direct referrals; pilot neighbourhood health centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan (urgent appointments, contract reform, supervised tooth‑brushing).
- National Care Service with national standards; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; right to family visits.
- 8,500 additional mental‑health staff; modernise Mental Health Act; public‑health actions on smoking, vaping, junk‑food ads and energy drinks; online‑safety and gambling reforms; reduce health inequalities; women’s health focus; end new HIV cases by 2030.

Governance and foreign policy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; restrict MPs’ paid consultancies; Commons modernisation.
- House of Lords: end hereditary seats, retirement at 80, participation rules; consult on a more representative replacement.
- Votes at 16; fix voter‑ID inconsistencies; tighter donation rules; reset intergovernmental relations and devolution.
- Foreign policy: reinforce alliances (NATO, AUKUS); sustained support for Ukraine and asset‑seizure efforts; remain in the ECHR; improve EU relations without re‑entering SM/CU/FoM (veterinary deal, MRAs, security pact); targeted trade strategy; Clean Power Alliance; rebuild development capacity with a path back to 0.7% when fiscal conditions allow.
